page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192 is a compute-focused server powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 192 virtual CPUs mapped to 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 720 GB of dedicated RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. It has a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4-standard-192 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read and write bandwidths for large blocks, alongside top-tier performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation. Single-core performance is moderately lower, ranking in the top 25% for Geekbench single-core and average for stress-ng single-core. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to top-tier performance in CPU encryption, physics simulations, and large-model LLM inference text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers high resource density and compute capacity for highly parallelized workloads without the added cost of GPU hardware. It is well-suited for compute-intensive tasks such as large-scale software compilation, multi-threaded data decompression, high-throughput web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference. The lack of local storage requires network-attached storage configurations, making it ideal for stateless compute nodes, distributed database operations, and parallel physics simulations.
